clue.text: Waste away although I arrived back and had some food

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for arrived from right to left

parts.note: arrived means came
had some food means ate

explanation.surface: Someone wasted away even though they turned up again and had a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CAME into EMAC; 'although' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To become emaciated is to grow abnormally thin, wasting away through hunger or illness.

clue.text: When it is out of order, please pass

indicators.note: out of order says the letters of please are jumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A polite request to pass something along when things are not working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges PLEASE; 'When it is' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that passes is said to elapse: both verbs describe time going by.

clue.text: Pieces of good fortune do not come singly

definitions.text: Pieces of good fortune do not come singly

parts.words: Pieces of good fortune do not come singly
parts.note: valuable possessions, each a piece of good fortune, usually spoken of in the plural, never one at a time

explanation.surface: A twist on the saying that misfortunes never come singly.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says troubles come in battalions; here the good things are plural too, as the word is almost always used in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Things of value one owns are lucky holdings, and the word is normally plural.

clue.text: Explain a correction of the printer, and in French as well

indicators.note: a correction of suggests the letters of printer are put right into a new order

parts.note: et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A request to account for a printer's correction, in French too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a correction of' rearranges PRINTER to INTERPR; 'the' and 'as well' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret something is to explain its meaning.

clue.text: Summons to drinking for a knight as a means of preparing food

parts.note: toasting is calling on everyone to raise a glass and drink
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A call to raise glasses to a knight, framed as a kitchen method.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled fork holds bread before a fire so it can be browned.

clue.text: Decoration of a law-giver

definitions.meaning: an ornamental picture made of small pieces of tile or glass
relating to Moses, who gave the Israelites their law

explanation.surface: A picture of ornament belonging to some ancient lawmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both inlaid tile decoration and pertaining to Moses, the biblical lawgiver.

clue.text: Place included among those which Lusaka sold up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
included among those words says the letters lie inside Lusaka sold

explanation.surface: A place that formed part of what was sold off in Zambia's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those which' is padding; the run AKASO sits inside 'Lusaka sold' and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a large Japanese city, so a place.

clue.text: Laxative that is taken by an unusual parent

indicators.note: taken by says one piece is swallowed into the other
unusual says the letters of parent are arranged in an odd way

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A laxative swallowed by a peculiar mother or father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' gives APERNT; 'taken by' signals the container. Aperients were a staple of the old family medicine cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperient medicine opens the bowels, acting as a mild purgative.

clue.text: Noblewoman who is against a thing of value going up

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up reverses the word read from bottom to top

parts.note: an asset is a thing of value

explanation.surface: A titled lady opposed to a valuable item rising in price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns ASSET into TESSA; 'who is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A contessa is an Italian countess, a woman of noble rank.

clue.text: I am in the devil's grip preceded by a liberal, being a dog

indicators.note: I am in the grip of says the letter I goes inside the devil's name

parts.note: Satan is the devil

explanation.surface: A self-confessed victim of the devil, introduced by a liberal, turns out to be a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grip' and 'preceded by' are links; I sits inside SATAN after A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alsatian is a German shepherd, a breed of dog.

clue.text: A famous day in the lake or inn

indicators.note: in says the day is placed inside the lake

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
VE Day, Victory in Europe Day in 1945

explanation.surface: Choosing whether to spend a celebrated day on the water or at a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: VE Day (8 May 1945) is famous in Britain; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is a pub or inn where drink is served.

clue.text: Proclamation the bottom half of which is something binding

definitions.text: Proclamation the bottom half of which is something binding

parts.words: Proclamation the bottom half of which is something binding
parts.note: a public statement whose final six letters spell a building material that sets hard and binds bricks

explanation.surface: A decree whose lower part contains a binding clause.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry the bottom half is CEMENT, which binds; the clue does not supply the first half, so the definition does that work.
explanation.definitionFit: A proclamation is a formal public statement.

clue.text: Instrument with which the great performer grips one

indicators.note: grips says the performer holds one inside

parts.note: a star is a great performer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instrument held tightly by a celebrated musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian stringed instrument.

clue.text: Cause torment at least in being crazy

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of at least in are jumbled

explanation.surface: Craziness, at the very least, torments people.
explanation.definitionFit: To tantalise is to torment with something kept just out of reach, like Tantalus.

clue.text: A Spaniard tries to talk with people who speak a different language

definitions.text: people who speak a different language

parts.note: General Franco, the Spanish dictator
phones means calls up to talk

explanation.surface: A Spaniard rings people who do not share his language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Francophones speak French, a different language from English.

clue.text: Order which gives greetings with a cherry pie

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: pie, as in printer's pie, means type jumbled together, so a cherry is mixed up

explanation.surface: An order that hands out hellos along with cherry pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' (printer's pie, a jumble of type) rearranges A CHERRY to ERARCHY; 'which gives' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarchy is an order of rank, one level above another.

clue.text: It secures dismissal and provides a period of relaxation

definitions.meaning: a cricket delivery spun from off to leg that can take a batsman's wicket
read as two words, a pause from work: time out

explanation.surface: Something that gets you sacked but also gives you time off.
explanation.walkthrough: An off-break is a spinning cricket ball that can get a batsman out; split, 'off break' is a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket ball dismisses batsmen, while an off break is a rest from duty.

clue.text: Daring amalgamation of two towns

annotationWithheld.why: Daring amalgamation of two towns (8): 'Daring' defines AUDACITY, but no reading of 'amalgamation of two towns' found gives AUDA + CITY or the whole word

clue.text: Little digit for one who points out a former Oxford degree

parts.note: Oxford once awarded fourth-class honours degrees
a finger points things out, and to finger is to identify

explanation.surface: The pinkie belongs to someone who identifies an old Oxford qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford awarded a fourth-class degree until the 1960s; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The little finger counts as the fourth finger after the thumb is excluded.

clue.text: Drink between two articles provided for pain

indicators.note: between says the drink sits among the articles

parts.note: an and a are both indefinite articles
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A drink with grammar on either side, offered as relief for an ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart.

clue.text: Plunder and escape this abroad

parts.note: flee means escape
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: Advice to rob and run away from this place overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to rob or swindle them.

clue.text: Restaurant with a lake behind the band

indicators.note: behind says the lake follows the band

parts.note: a brass band
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: An eatery by the water, with the band playing at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style restaurant.

clue.text: Polish part of the capital

explanation.surface: A Polish district in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheen (East Sheen) is a district of south-west London; 'Polish' is the noun meaning shine, not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means gloss, and also names a London suburb.

clue.text: Book without an article or make a cancellation

indicators.note: without says the article is left out of the book

parts.note: an annual is a yearly book
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A yearly publication cancelled for lack of an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to cancel or declare void.

clue.text: Worked for the press and had a belief without little credit

indicators.note: without says the abbreviation is removed from the longer word

parts.note: credited means believed
CR is the abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A journalist believed a story without much acknowledgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Edited material has been revised and prepared for publication.

clue.text: Tell how one cries uncontrollably in a strange bed

indicators.note: in says one jumble sits inside the other
strange says the letters of bed are rearranged
uncontrollably says the letters of cries are thrown about

explanation.surface: Explaining how a person weeps without restraint in an unfamiliar bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagram signals, 'strange' and 'uncontrollably', each scramble their own word before one goes inside the other; 'how one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To describe something is to give an account of it in words.

clue.text: Principle held by cask for regulating pitch

indicators.note: held by says the principle goes inside the cask

parts.note: a keg is a small cask
yin is the Chinese feminine principle

explanation.surface: A principle contained in a barrel, used for tuning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Keying sets an instrument or voice to a particular key or tone.

clue.text: As a means of keeping one in Yale acts absurdly

definitions.text: a means of keeping one in

indicators.note: absurdly says the letters of Yale acts are rearranged ridiculously

explanation.surface: A Yale lock behaving foolishly as a way of keeping someone inside.
explanation.walkthrough: A staylace laces up a corset (stays), keeping the wearer in; 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The lace tightens a corset that holds the figure firmly.
